To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brand loyalty, size loyalties and price sensitivity are higher in the online channel for grocery products than in the offline store.

the online channel is more brand loyal but less price competitive than the offline channel, that online shoppers are more brand loyal and size loyal but less sensitive to price than offline shoppers, that light online shoppers are more loyal and less sensitive to price in the online channel, and that the online channel exhibits larger brand loyalty and price competition than the offline channel for food products.

brand loyalty, size loyalties and price sensitivities differ across channels and are closely related to shopping frequency and household characteristics, and that the differences across channels are larger for food and sensory products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the moderating effects that household and product characteristics have on shopping behavior across online and offline stores.
the online–offline differences and moderating household and product effects in shopping behavior for grocery products.
the online–offline channel differences in shopping behavior across households, products and channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the moderating effects are significant, but not uniform across all household and product characteristics.
online shopping behavior for grocery products is more brand and size loyal but less sensitive to price than offline shopping behavior.
the online and offline channels are complementary in terms of household brand loyalty and size loyalty, but competing in terms of household price sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
online shopping behavior is different from offline shopping behavior and that these differences depend upon household characteristics, product characteristics and the level of online shopping.
online and offline channels have different effects on household shopping behavior across product categories.

the online channel is more effective in attracting and retaining loyal customers for grocery products than the offline channel, but the offline channel is more effective for price promotions for grocery products than online.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online and offline channels should not be viewed in isolation but rather as a single integrated channel.
the online–offline differences are not uniform across households, but are strongly influenced by the shopping behavior of households and by the product characteristics.
the online and offline shopping behavior of the households is heterogeneous and depends on their shopping frequency and the nature of the products.
